title: Optimize symbol resolution paths and compatibility testing for GPU kernels
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We see sporadic slow node startup and rare symbol resolution failures when loading GPU kernel bundles across heterogeneous fleets (A100/H100/RTX). This ticket consolidates a pragmatic refactor of the symbol resolution path: reduce redundant dlopen/dlsym passes, add deterministic prelink ordering for CUTLASS and Triton plugin artifacts, and add a compatibility test matrix and CI canary to catch regressions. Goal: reduce cold-start symbol resolution latency and eliminate flaky missing-symbol errors observed during live rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: Average GPU runtime startup time for a cold worker (first model invocation) drops from 420ms to <= 220ms across A100/H100 nodes measured by runtime-startup-dashboard
No missing-symbol errors in canary fleet for 72h after rollout across at least 3 different CUDA driver versions
CI matrix covers CUDA 12.4/12.6/13.0, Triton v2.x-3.x, CUTLASS v2/v3 with deterministic pass/fail reproduction
Automated rollback hooks added to rollout orchestration when symbol resolution errors exceed 0.1% of requests in a 15 minute window
steps: Audit current dynamic loader usage: enumerate all dlopen/dlsym calls and shared object open paths in the runtime and quant loaders
Introduce ordered prelink manifest for kernel bundles (manifest entries: soname, major-version, preferred-path) and load according to manifest instead of glob ordering
Deduplicate symbol lookups by introducing a short-lived symbol cache keyed by (soname, symbol) scoped to process startup
Add load-time diagnostic telemetry and trace IDs so failing loads emit reproducible artifact fingerprints
Implement a fallback resolver that only triggers when manifest load fails and records a diagnostic bundle for post-mortem
Create reproducible unit and integration tests that emulate missing symbol scenarios and verify fallback behaviour
Add CI job with matrix (CUDA/Triton/CUTLASS combos) and a canary rollout pipeline that exercises real inference flows for 24-72h
testing_notes: Local repro harness: scripts/test_symbol_repro.sh accepts --cuda-driver, --model, --bundle-path and runs 50 cold starts recording dlopen traces
Use perf-counter tagging to correlate startup latency to symbol lookup counts and dlopen timeouts
Manual validation on H100 (driver 535.86) and A100 (driver 525.85) available in infra/gpu-lab
Set CI thresholds: fail on >5% cold-start regressions relative to baseline for the same commit range

rollout_plan: Phase 1: land change behind feature flag and run CI matrix; Phase 2: deploy to canary pool (5% of capacity) for 48h with telemetry alerts; Phase 3: expand to 30% for 24h; Phase 4: full fleet. Automatic rollback if symbol errors > 0.1% or cold-start regression > 10% vs canary baseline.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: prelink manifest could increase chance of missing alternate library paths on custom customer images. Mitigation: keep fallback path resolution enabled and log missing manifests for 2 weeks before enforcing strict manifest only mode
Risk: aggressive symbol caching may mask library load-time updates during hot-restart. Mitigation: cache TTL of 5 minutes and explicit cache invalidation on process-restart signal
Risk: CI matrix increases pipeline time. Mitigation: run full matrix on merge, and a trimmed smoke matrix on PRs; cache binary artifacts between runs
perf_targets: Target: reduce median symbol lookup time per process from 35ms to <10ms
Target: reduce number of dlopen calls per cold-start from median 12 to <=4
Target: reduce observed cold-start P95 from 820ms to <=480ms
notes_on_tradeoffs: We prefer a modest engineering change (manifest + small cache) rather than large refactor of runtime loader to minimize risk and rollout complexity
Strict manifest-only loading gives stronger determinism but reduces compatibility with customer-provided custom library layouts; approach is to gate strict mode behind a runtime flag
The symbol cache trades a slight window of stale resolution for large reductions in repeated lookup cost; the TTL keeps the stale window bounded
